llms.body:
# Crossref

> Crossref is a not-for-profit membership organisation that runs open infrastructure for research. Members (publishers, funders, universities, and others) register DOIs and metadata for their research outputs with Crossref. The metadata is openly available for anyone to use via APIs and bulk data files. Crossref does not assess the quality of research or peer review: a Crossref DOI shows that a record exists, not that the work is trustworthy.

Key facts:
- Organisations join as members. Individuals can't join directly.
- Organisations in eligible countries may qualify for reduced or waived fees through the GEM program, or can join through a sponsor.
- To check whether a DOI is real, resolve it at https://doi.org/ or look it up via Crossref's search tool or REST API.
- Retractions and corrections are available in the metadata, including the Retraction Watch database.

## About Crossref
- [About](https://www.crossref.org/about/): who we are, what we do, governance
- [Strategy](https://www.crossref.org/strategy/): our direction and priorities
- [Operations and sustainability](https://www.crossref.org/operations-and-sustainability/): finances, annual reports, policies

## Joining and fees
- [Membership](https://www.crossref.org/membership/): who can join and how
- [Fees](https://www.crossref.org/fees/): current annual membership and DOI registration fees
- [GEM program](https://www.crossref.org/gem/): fee waivers and reductions by country
- [Working with a sponsor](https://www.crossref.org/membership/about-sponsors/): joining through a sponsoring organisation

## Registering and maintaining DOI records
- [Documentation home](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/)
- [Getting set up as a member](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/member-setup/)
- [Ways to register records](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/register-maintain-records/choose-content-registration-method/)
- [OJS plugin](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/register-maintain-records/ojs-plugin/)
- [Record types and best practice](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/principles-practices/): journals, books, preprints, datasets, grants, peer reviews and more

## Using Crossref metadata
- [REST API](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/rest-api/): free public API; include a mailto for the polite pool
- [Bulk data downloads](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/bulk-downloads/): annual public data file, updated around April each year
- [Retraction Watch data](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/retraction-watch/)
- [Text and data mining](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/retrieve-metadata/text-and-data-mining/)
- [Metadata Plus](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/metadata-plus/): paid service with greater support, monthly data files, higher rate limits, and an SLA

## Optional
- [Blog](https://www.crossref.org/blog/): news and analysis; older posts may be out of date, so check the documentation for current processes about Crossref services
- [Community forum](https://community.crossref.org/)

Latest blog posts
2026 October 20

Share your research integrity experiences with Crossref and STM

As we approach the end of 2026, research integrity remains a critical focus for the scholarly publishing ecosystem: fast technological advancements are constantly pushing the boundaries of integrity, impacting how everyone in this space interacts with the scholarly record.

...Find out more
2026 October 06

How Grobid uses Crossref metadata to enrich bibliographic information

Crossref members register around 37,000 records daily. All this metadata is openly shared with the global scholarly community through our free APIs. We receive over two billion calls to our API each month, signalling its use by hundreds of tools and services worldwide, supporting the discovery and assessment of scholarly metadata. As part of a new series in our blog, we will spotlight the diversity of tools and integrations that rely on Crossref metadata to serve the scholarly community. In this initial post, we chat to Luca Foppiano, the developer and maintainer of Grobid1, to learn about how Grobid uses Crossref metadata to improve the extraction and enrichment of bibliographic information from scholarly PDFs.

...Find out more
2026 September 21

2026 board election slate

On behalf of the Nominating Committee, I’m pleased to share the slate of candidates for the 2026 board election. Every active member organisation is invited to submit a ballot to elect the incoming board class.

...Find out more
2026 September 17

July 2026 board meeting summary

We’re providing a summary of the board’s July 2026 meeting. The July board meeting is our only in-person meeting. The board gathers for two days of strategic thinking and long-range planning, as well as conducting annual board business. This year, we focused on allocating surplus funds we have on hand to invest in a three-year project to redesign the content system. In a related discussion, we decided to lower content registration fees starting in 2027 because we’ve had a demonstrated history of generating surpluses, exceeding what we need to run Crossref. We also discussed the board structure, as part of our regular review of stakeholder governance. And we conducted annual board business, such as approving the audited financial statements and reviewed our risk register and mitigation plans.

The resolutions are available on the dedicated section of our website, which also lists the members of the Board and offers further information about our governance.

We also managed to squeeze in watching a World Cup game over dinner.

...Find out more

We run the open infrastructure to link research objects, entities, and actions—creating a lasting and reusable scholarly record that underpins open science.

Together with our >26,500 members in 171 countries, we drive metadata exchange and support 2.1 billion monthly API queries, facilitating global research communication, for the benefit of society.
